key_insight: In a large health check-up cohort, chest X-ray AI aligned well with routine radiologist reads and was especially sensitive for nodules/masses, with retrospective hints of earlier lung cancer flagging in some cases.
clinical_relevance: This suggests AI could support chest radiograph screening workflows by helping prioritize suspicious cases, but prospective validation is still needed before clinical benefit can be claimed.
method: 298,991 consecutive chest radiographs from 114,866 people in a single-center health check-up cohort (2019–2023).
Compared a commercial AI system against routine double-reading radiologist interpretation using two preset positivity rules: any of 10 findings, and nodule/mass only.
Retrospectively reviewed 48 histopathologically confirmed lung cancer cases for timeline comparison of AI vs radiologist positivity.
evidence_signal: Using radiologist-referenced analysis, AI showed 72.0% sensitivity and 79.6% specificity for all findings, and 87.1% sensitivity and 91.8% specificity for nodule/mass; negative predictive values were 99.0% and 100.0%.
watch_item: Because the study used radiologist judgment rather than universal CT or pathology verification as the main reference, the results reflect operational concordance and exploratory retrospective findings rather than proven patient outcome benefit.
paper_title: Chest Radiography AI Concordance and Lung Cancer Linkage in a Large Health Check-up Cohort
